descricao_original: Macrophages are the major phagocytic cell in connective tissue. They are derived from blood-borne monocytes (upper left) that migrate into the tissue (two lower left panels). The ultrastructure of a macrophage is shown on the right. Macrophage nuclei are oval-shaped and frequently indented, reflecting the cell’s origin from a monocyte. The pink cytoplasm, when visible, contains numerous lysosomes and phagocytosed material. 1000x (LM), 8000x (EM)
